answers.explanation: Submit and come back later: batch.
Interactive use by many people at once is timesharing.
Swapping moves processes in and out of memory.
CPU scheduling chooses among ready processes.
Timesharing adds regular short time slices on top of that.
Each job alone keeps the CPU busy 1 ms in 5, or 20%. Two jobs that never collide give 40%.
Only part of the process needs to be in memory at a time.
